title: Password Pusher
name: password-pusher
description: Share passwords, text, files and links as a link that expires after a set number of views or days, so they don't sit in someone's chat history or inbox forever. Source: https://github.com/pglombardo/PasswordPusher

env.name: PWPUSH_MASTER_KEY
env.label: Master key (required)
env.description: Encrypts the text of every push. Exactly 64 hex characters, so generate it with: openssl rand -hex 32. Keep it the same when you redeploy, or older pushes can't be opened.

env.name: PWPUSH_SECRET_KEY_BASE
env.label: Login key
env.description: Keeps people logged in through a restart. Generate one with: openssl rand -hex 64. Leave it blank and every restart logs everyone out.

env.name: PWPUSH_PORT
env.label: Host port for the web UI

note: Set the master key before you deploy (openssl rand -hex 32 makes one), since the stack won't start without it. Then open http://<your-host>:5150 (or whichever port you picked), which goes straight to a first-run page for the admin account. It wants a boot code from the container's logs: search them for Boot Code. After that, anyone who can reach it can push without an account, and sign up for one too. To stop either, add PWPUSH_ANONYMOUS = false or PWPUSH_DISABLE_SIGNUPS = true to the stack's environment variables and redeploy. Pushes, files and accounts live in the pwpush-storage volume. Text is encrypted with the master key there, but uploaded files are kept as they are. Docs: docs.pwpush.com
